description: Start() must initialize gameplay state, pooled objects, camera/background. Game end flow must call GameEnded() then ShowCTA() with InstallFullGame(). Phase count in CheckEventRules() must match spec exactly — CUA verifies per-phase coverage.
rule: Code Completeness
fix: 1) Initialize state/pool objects/camera in Start(), move >=3 pool objects to visible positions. 2) In gameEnd: call GameEnded() first, then ShowCTA() which calls InstallFullGame(). 3) ruleTriggered[] must have exactly as many entries as spec phases, each with real per-phase conditions.

description: Phase coverage incomplete — CUA detects 0 or near-0 phases completed. Usually means auto-progression bypassed intermediate phases or phase transition conditions are trivial/timer-only.
rule: CUA Verification
fix: Ensure every phase has real player-driven transition conditions (not timer-only). Verify ruleTriggered[] array covers ALL spec phases. Check that AddCompletedPhase/ReportPhase is called for each phase.

description: Forbidden runtime APIs: Application.ExternalEval() unsupported in Luna. GFM_UI.CreateText + Destroy() produces invisible/broken text. Never Destroy UI elements — hide by moving off-screen.
rule: Forbidden APIs
fix: 1) Remove ExternalEval — use supported Luna/GFM mechanisms. 2) Pre-create reusable text labels (or use skeleton guideText/scoreText) and update content. Never Destroy UI — hide via (0,-999,0).

description: Skeleton pre-creates uiCanvas, guideText, scoreText — use those directly instead of creating new UI structures at runtime. Runtime GFM_UI.CreateCanvas/CreateText may be invisible in Luna.
rule: GFM_Tools API Signatures
fix: Use existing skeleton-provided UI variables. If CTA button needed, use skeleton CTAButton pattern. Only create new UI if skeleton doesn't provide the element.

description: SafeColor or similar helper implemented as infinite recursion — calls itself unconditionally. Stack overflow causes immediate blank screen.
rule: Materials & Rendering
fix: Ensure color/material helper functions have proper base cases. Colors are pre-baked in pool objects — no runtime color manipulation needed.

description: Camera.backgroundColor too close to ground color — difference < 0.3 on all RGB channels triggers solid-color-screen detection. Recommended: camera (0.35, 0.55, 0.75) deep sky blue, ground (0.75, 0.78, 0.82) neutral gray.
rule: Solid-Color Screen Prevention
fix: Set Camera.backgroundColor to (0.35f, 0.55f, 0.75f). Set ground color to (0.75f, 0.78f, 0.82f). Ensure >=0.3 difference on at least one RGB channel.

description: Template has 160 pre-baked colored pool objects named __Pool_{Shape}_{Color}_{NN}. Colors are baked in URP/Lit materials. Never use GFM_Create.SetColor() — it causes GL_INVALID_OPERATION.
rule: Pre-Baked Color Pool
fix: Use GameObject.Find("__Pool_Cube_Red_01") to get a red cube. Available shapes: Cube, Sphere, Cylinder, Plane. Available colors: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Purple, White, Brown, Cyan, Pink.

description: Bridge.NET throws 'Class already defined' if GameFlowManagerMain is defined twice. Template engine already has a stub — build pipeline strips it in assembleStage4().
rule: Luna 7.1.0 Engine Compatibility
fix: Do not define duplicate class names. The build pipeline handles stub stripping automatically.

description: CTA button must have one-time creation guard. Without ctaBtn==null check, repeated calls create duplicate buttons. Prefer skeleton-provided CTAButton pattern.
rule: Common Mistakes
fix: Guard button creation with if (ctaBtn == null). Prefer skeleton-provided UI flow over runtime GFM_UI.CreateButton.

description: Random.Range in runtime spawning/movement creates nondeterministic CUA verification paths. Phase progression tied to random timing makes CUA coverage unreliable.
rule: Gameplay Logic
fix: Make phase transitions depend on explicit player-driven events (click/drag/move), not random spawn counts or timing. Minimize Random.Range in gameplay-critical paths.

description: Input.GetMouseButtonDown(0) alone may fail on mobile. Luna/GFM input abstraction or explicit touch+mouse dual handling required.
rule: Luna Platform Limitations
fix: Handle both touch and mouse input. Use GFM/Luna input abstraction when available. Avoid dependence on physics raycasts — convert screen input to world position via camera math.

description: Phase progression must be driven by player interaction, not enemy spawner counters or auto-timers. enemySpawnCount or similar NPC-driven counters should not gate phase transitions.
rule: Architecture
fix: Gate phase transitions on player accomplishments (entities built, items collected by player action). Align RULE_COUNT with actual spec phase count.

description: Uses List/Dictionary-safe style correctly, but still uses generic syntax indirectly via arrays only; no issue there. Actual critical issue is elsewhere: the code creates runtime UI button instances in gameplay flow, which is not prohibited by itself, but the skeleton note explicitly says pre-created uiCanvas/guideText/scoreText should be used instead of creating new UI structures. More importantly, phase coverage is incomplete versus the validated 11-phase hospital/station management spec in the auto-promoted rules.
rule: c language  bridge.net hard limits
fix: Implement the full required spec phase set in CheckEventRules() instead of compressing progression into 6 gameplay phases.

description: Uses color-suffixed pool names like __Pool_Plane_Green_01, __Pool_Cube_Blue_01, __Pool_Cylinder_Purple_01, etc. The documented required pool names are shape-only names such as __Pool_Cube_01..50, __Pool_Sphere_01..20, __Pool_Plane_01..10, __Pool_Cylinder_01..10. Under the stated rules these names do not exist, so Find will return null and cause runtime failure.
rule: object naming  pool objects
fix: Replace every Find string with exact existing pool object names from the allowed numeric pool set, using explicit string literals or a predeclared exact-name array. Null-check every required object after Find.

description: Phase 4 transitions on firstCrewDelivered == true and phaseTimer >= 4f. firstCrewDelivered is commented as 'set when first crew is picked up', while the phase description requires treating rescued crew / collecting gold. This is not a real phase-specific completion check for treatment and can skip based on prior rescue state rather than current player action.
rule: every phase must have real completion conditions  phase progression must require
fix: Gate the transition on a true treatment interaction state specific to this phase, such as crew healed in bathroom by player-delivered rescue flow plus required gold interaction flag.

description: Phase 5 requires carryCapacityState >= 3, but in this file carryCapacityState is never modified. The comments say it is 'Set when player purchases carry upgrade', but no such assignment exists in the provided code. As reviewed, phase progression is incomplete and will stall.
rule: variables referenced in trigger conditions must be modified somewhere in update
fix: Ensure carryCapacityState is explicitly assigned during the carry-upgrade interaction logic, e.g. in UpdateCarryUpgradeClick() or another provided helper method.

description: The skeleton explicitly says Camera.backgroundColor is pre-set to (0.45, 0.52, 0.62) and must not be changed. The code changes it again to (0.35, 0.55, 0.75). Even if the latter is generally recommended, this file's skeleton forbids modifying that preset.
rule: skeleton line  auto-promoted critical camera-background rule
fix: Remove the later backgroundColor assignment and keep the skeleton-provided value unchanged.

description: Calls GFM_Create.InitMaterialFromScene(). This API is explicitly forbidden/obsolete in the provided Luna rules and should not be used because pool object colors are pre-baked.
rule: forbidden legacy apis  forbidden runtime apis
fix: Remove GFM_Create.InitMaterialFromScene() entirely.

description: The "data" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer, TypedArray, or DataView. Received an instance of Object
rule: interaction  gameplay
fix: Investigate why phase "unknown" is never reached. The transition condition or interaction handler is likely broken.

description: Phase 2 initialization incorrectly calls AddCompletedPhase("phase_1775610864395_1") instead of marking the current phase or the correct transition semantics. Similar pattern repeats for later phases, always adding the previous phase ID during the next phase init. This produces inaccurate completedPhases tracking and can break CUA phase coverage validation.
rule: phase id format  phase completion tracking correctness
fix: When a phase is actually completed, call AddCompletedPhase() with that exact phase's Rule ID at the correct completion point. Do not duplicate prior phase IDs during next-phase initialization.

description: Phase 5 transitions when firstCrewTreated == true and gold >= 30 and phaseTimer threshold is met. There is no explicit interaction flag in the condition despite the phase spec requiring player action. This allows progression based purely on accumulated state once thresholds are met.
rule: phase transition must require real player interaction not just timerstate
fix: Add a true player interaction requirement for this transition, such as a treatment interaction flag and/or gold collection interaction flag that is set only by player action.

description: Phase 10 transitions only on restBedState >= 2 and phaseTimer threshold. This is not a real completion condition for 'base stable operation' and can advance without the required player-driven gold collection objective.
rule: every ruletriggeredn block must have a real completion condition tied to player
fix: Require a real player accomplishment for Phase 10, such as player-collected gold threshold and a specific interaction flag, not merely restBedState.

description: Several trigger variables are referenced for progression—firstCrewTreated, batchRescueDone, bathroomCapacityState, secondCabinState, restBedState, carryCapacityState, downloadButtonDone, unlockButtonDone, screenDone, playerDone, goldDone—but this file does not show any assignments updating them except resets. Under the mechanical verification rule, progression variables used in CheckEventRules() must be modified somewhere in Update() or helper logic; as reviewed here, the implementation is incomplete and likely stalls.
rule: variables referenced in trigger conditions must be declared and modified somewhe
fix: Implement explicit state mutations in the gameplay handlers/helper methods and ensure those methods are present and actually called from Update().

description: Several progression flags are satisfied by UpdateAutoPlay() without real user input, including screenDone, upgrade completion flags, build flags, and final downloadButtonDone/phase11InteractDone. This creates non-interactive scripted advancement paths.
rule: phase progression must be driven by player interaction never auto-advance via sc
fix: Delete auto-setting of any progression flag from non-user-driven code paths. Only actual input handlers should set interaction flags.

description: The code records AddCompletedPhase("gameStart") for phase 1, which is not a valid blueprint Rule ID. It also marks prior phase IDs during next-phase initialization rather than at the actual completion moment. This breaks phase coverage tracking and violates the required exact Rule ID usage.
rule: phase id format critical  addcompletedphase parameter must exactly match bluepri
fix: Call AddCompletedPhase() only when that exact phase is completed, using the exact Rule ID string for that phase. Remove "gameStart" and stop recording previous phases during next-phase setup.

description: Uses UnityEngine.Debug.Log() for phase/state reporting during gameplay flow. While not the highest-level forbidden API, this is a known Luna production risk, and UpdateGameState() is called repeatedly from Start, transitions, and periodic Update. Console spam can destabilize playable verification.
rule: common production failure  performance-safe skeleton usage
fix: Remove Debug.Log-based phase/state reporting from runtime flow, or guard it behind a compile-time debug flag excluded from Luna builds.

description: Creates runtime UI text with GFM_UI.CreateText for floatingText. Runtime text creation is called out as a production risk in the provided rules, and the skeleton specifically prefers pre-created reusable UI instead of creating new text elements at runtime.
rule: forbidden runtime apis  skeleton ui rule
fix: Reuse an existing pre-created text element or add a skeleton-provided pooled text reference. Do not create Text at runtime in gameplay flow.

description: AddCompletedPhase uses semantic names like "openingDisaster", "unlockCabinDoor", "placeCrewToBath", "unlockFirstBed", "unlockAllBeds", "finalCTA", and also records prior phases during next-phase init. Project rules require exact blueprint Rule IDs only, and only when that exact phase completes.
rule: phase id format  exact rule ids required
fix: Replace all AddCompletedPhase parameters with the exact blueprint Rule ID strings and record them at the actual completion moment for that phase only.

description: The code marks previous phases as completed during the next phase's initialization, e.g. phase 2 adds openingDisaster, phase 3 adds unlockMainCabinDoor, etc. Historical failure rule explicitly flags this pattern as invalid because completion must be recorded at the actual completion moment, not when entering the next phase.
rule: addcompletedphase timing correctness
fix: Move each AddCompletedPhase() call into the exact transition point where that phase's completion condition becomes true.

description: Phase 1 init explicitly sets openingDisasterInteractionDone = true without any user interaction. The rules say anti-autoplay flags must be set when the player performs the required interaction; auto-setting them is forbidden.
rule: every phase transition must require player interaction never auto-set interactio
fix: Set openingDisasterInteractionDone only from a real input handler, e.g. first joystick move or first tap.

description: AutoPlay directly mutates progression resources/state (ice, water, oxygen, gold) based on currentPhaseName instead of performing real player-equivalent interactions through gameplay handlers. This creates scripted advancement paths rather than real interaction-driven progression.
rule: forbidden autoplay state mutation bypassing interaction
fix: Refactor AutoPlay to drive the player to targets and trigger the same input/interaction functions used by the player, without directly assigning progression state.

description: Phase 10 requires drillState >= 3 and upgradeStationDone == true, but in the provided file drillState is never set to 3 anywhere, and upgradeStationDone is never assigned true anywhere. As reviewed, progression will stall before phase 10.
rule: variables referenced in trigger conditions must be modified somewhere
fix: Implement ShowDownloadButton() and a real click handler that sets downloadCtaDone = true on user interaction, or wire the CTA to an existing skeleton CTA pattern.

description: The AutoPlay safety net directly mutates progression flags and entity states for stuck phases: openingDisasterInteractionDone, mainCabinDoorState, phase3FirstCrewRescueDone, phase4CrewDeliveredDone, carryAbilityState, bathtubState, secondCabinState, firstBedUnlockButtonDone, phase10AllBedsDone, downloadButtonDone, etc. The rules explicitly forbid scripted auto-completion paths and require player-driven interaction conditions, even for verification.
rule: tier 1.4b  every phase must have real completion conditions progression must req
fix: Do not directly set progression flags/entity terminal states in the safety net. AutoPlay must drive the same interaction handlers as the player, not assign completion state variables.

description: AutoPlay arrival directly sets phase-completion flags such as cabinDoorUnlockButtonDone, floatingCrewDone, phase4CrewDeliveredDone, phase3FirstCrewRescueDone, crewDone, phase6BatchRescueDone, firstBedUnlockButtonDone, phase9FirstBedDone, restBedUnlockButtonDone, phase10AllBedsDone, and downloadButtonDone. This is explicit autoplay progression, which the rules forbid.
rule: tier 1.4b  every phase must have real condition not scripted flag mutation
fix: Refactor AutoPlay so it invokes the same user-input-driven interaction methods used in interactive mode instead of directly toggling progression flags.

description: Entity state variables are declared as 0=waiting, 1=building, 2=built, but transitions check for >=3 on carryAbilityState and bathtubState, and later safety net sets restBedState = 6. This breaks the documented state model and indicates inconsistent/incomplete phase logic.
rule: tier 1.4b  variables referenced in trigger conditions must be modified somewhere
fix: Use a consistent state model. If upgrade levels need 3, declare separate level variables and update them through real interaction handlers. Keep entity state variables within their declared domain.

description: AutoPlay directly mutates progression state and phase-completion flags/resources (ice, water, oxygen, gold, techConsoleDone, recruitConsoleDone, incubatorConsoleDone, upgradeStationDone, unlockNewCabinCtaDone, downloadCtaDone, etc.). The safety net also force-sets completion variables like iceOreDone=true, unloadingAreaDone=true, electrolysisStartButtonDone=true, sellAreaDone=true. This is explicit scripted advancement rather than player-driven interaction.
rule: tier 1  4b  tier 1 anti-autoplay every phase must require real player interactio
fix: Remove direct state-completion mutations from OnAutoPlayArrive and the safety net. AutoPlay must drive the same input/interaction handlers as the player, not assign completion flags or terminal entity states directly.

description: AddCompletedPhase uses semantic names like "landSpaceshipMoveToEntrance", "collectIceOre", "deliverIceToSmelter", "produceOxygenByElectrolyzer", "sellOxygenEarnGold", "unlockAdvancedDrill", "unlockAutoVendorWorker", "ctaUnlockNewCabin", and "gameEndRedirectDownload" instead of exact blueprint Rule IDs.
rule: tier 1  11 addcompletedphase parameter must exactly match blueprint rule id
fix: Replace every AddCompletedPhase argument with the exact blueprint Rule ID strings provided by the spec, and record them only at the true completion point of that phase.

description: Phase 1 completion is based on player z-position > 2f, but OnAutoPlayArrive directly teleports the player beyond the entrance and the safety net also force-sets spaceStationEntranceDone=true. This allows non-interactive scripted completion of the first required player-action phase.
rule: tier 1  4b completion conditions must be phase-specific and player-driven
fix: Do not teleport/set the completion flag directly in autoplay. Route autoplay through actual movement/input behavior and only set the flag when that movement genuinely reaches the target.

description: AutoPlay directly invokes progression handlers from non-user-driven code paths to force phase completion. Historical rules explicitly flag this pattern as invalid autoplay/scripted advancement because phase progression must be driven by actual interaction handlers, not safety-net automation that sets completion variables for stuck phases.
rule: tier 1 rule 4b  tier 1 completeness  player-action-driven phases
fix: Remove safety-net completion of progression flags/states. AutoPlay must drive the same movement/input interaction flow without directly forcing completion, and phase gates must depend on genuine interaction state changes.
